newsitem.title: GERMANY: German regional metal workers gear up for strikes.
newsitem.headline: German regional metal workers gear up for strikes.

text.p: Two of the largest regional branches of the IG Metall trade union were on Tuesday making preparations necessary to launch strikes from March next year after talks aimed at solving a row on sick pay collapsed.

Representatives of the metal and engineering union in the southern state of Bavaria, home to industrial giants including Siemens and car-makers BMW and Volkswagen's Audi, said they were gearing up for strikes.
"We have a free hand from March 1 onwards," IG Metall official Richard Poltzmacher said in response to enquiries, adding that the union was already examining "strike methods".

Poltzmacher was speaking after the collapse of overnight talks in the region of North Rhine-Westphalia on the issue of sick pay, where employers are determined to find savings in accordance with a new law.
IG Metall Bavaria, which represents around half the region's 700,000 metal and engineering workers, has already stated it plans to cancel wage agreements in the region early next year.
All-out strikes are then possible under German law after a four-week mandatory cooling-off period following the termination of contracts.

Union officials in North-Rhine Westphalia, Germany's major steel-making region employing over 800,000 workers, are due to meet later on Tuesday and are widely expected to follow their Bavarian colleagues in agreeing plans to cancel wage contracts.
IG Metall, Germany's most powerful union with membership of close to three million, said the North Rhine-Westphalia talks represented for it the last attempt to reach a "pilot agreement" on sick pay.
IG Metall deputy chairman Walter Riester said on Tuesday that the issue would now have to be discussed within the regular 1997 wage round, due to start in regional committees from next month.
A similar attempt to find an agreement in the south-west region of Baden-Wuerttemberg also failed earlier this month.
IG Metall's last strike in 1993 involved some 40,000 east German metal and engineering workers in protests over wages in the former communist region.
